statement: A partition write that is rerouted or retried after an honest 'outcome unknown' answer must apply exactly once and answer the client the truth. Today (integrated head 7e08cefcd, round-5 r5-g2-dup and round-7 evidence): the distributed write coordinator mints a per-plan participant entryId, but the transport query reply (partition-service-entry-apply-base.js handleRemoteQuery) drops failureCode, retryAfterMs, consensus and entryId, so every remote consumer is text-only by construction; the query executor's system-table widening (query-executor-write-retry-routing.js:462,540), the CDC routed-mutation loop, the CDC local lane and the rebalancer mutation loops re-issue a write under a fresh identity, so an UPDATE released as outcome_unknown is applied twice on every replica and an INSERT answers a constraint error although the row exists; a replay reaches the client as success with changes 0; SQLQueryEngine drops a client-supplied idempotencyKey; the admin write receipt marks a replayed answer complete only when the answering replica claims leadership (F-w); the control-plane classifier does not walk participantResults and treats the post-commit environmental application failure as failed-for-good (F-as, F-at). After this quest: the write identity is minted at exactly one boundary per path (the engine for client statements; once per logical mutation for the CDC and rebalancer loops) and carried unchanged on every reroute or retry; the partition answers a same-entryId retry from the durable outcome row (idempotentReplay, the original affected-row count); write answers cross the wire whole, and reroute admission is by the kernel's code predicate with carriesEntryId, with no text fallback for a partition answer; the admin receipt binds a replayed answer by (partitionId, entryId, term, logIndex) and the replay flag; the classifier walks participant results and lists the post-commit environmental failure with the not-failed-for-good answers; the registry names every consumer of the write-answer classification.

constraints.statement: The write identity is minted at exactly one boundary per path (the SQL engine for client statements; once per logical mutation, outside the attempt loop, for the CDC routed mutation, the CDC local lane and the rebalancer mutation gateway). No downstream retry, reroute, widening or handoff mints a second identity; a client-supplied idempotencyKey reaches the coordinator's derivation unchanged.

A partition write answer is classified and rerouted by its failureCode through the kernel's predicates (isRetryableWriteFailureCode, isReroutableWriteFailureCode with carriesEntryId); the transport query reply carries the answer whole (failureCode, retryAfterMs, consensus, entryId, idempotentReplay, logIndex, replayOfLogIndex, changes). REROUTABLE_WRITE_ERROR_FRAGMENTS / isReroutableWriteError and their text consumers are deleted only when the static census of text consumers is zero; a remaining text consumer is a recorded finding, never a silent fallback.

No deadline, attempt count or retry budget is raised (the 30 s pending-commit deadline, the CDC and rebalancer attempt bounds stay); the replica-operation INSERT UNIQUE-collision patch is retired only when its red-on-revert witness shows the identity contract covers it.

Owners touched: src/query (engine, executor routing, request builders), the transport query reply in the partition owner, the CDC and rebalancer retry loops, the admin write receipt, the control-plane classifier, src/constants/errors.js and the write kernel's predicates; the frozen operation port, the runtime owner and the durable outcome row's schema are not changed (the row may gain the affected-row count as a recorded widening).
